text:
Dallas won 4-0 in Buffalo, and by the numbers it was the wrong team that walked away with the shutout. The Sabres out-attempted the Stars 63 to 39 and held the edge in expected goals, 2.37 to 2.10, a gap that widens to 2.17 to 1.36 at even strength. The simulated replays of every shot give Buffalo the win 55 percent of the time. Instead, the game turned in a 6 minute, 31 second stretch of the second period.

Jason Robertson opened the scoring in the first on a snap shot that carried only a 9 percent chance, and Sam Steel made it 2-0 early in the second on a 5 percent look. Then Mikko Rantanen added a backhand at 13:57, a 23 percent chance, and Roope Hintz converted a power play snap shot at 15:34. Four goals came from a combined 2.10 expected goals, and Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen finished 1.9 goals worse than expected on 18 shots. Rantanen had a goal and three assists, Wyatt Johnston three assists, and the Stars took the second period 1.20 to 0.59 in expected goals, which is where the lead was built.

Buffalo's pressure arrived too late. The Sabres controlled the third, out-chancing Dallas 1.36 to 0.29, with Tage Thompson putting six shots on net. But Jake Oettinger stopped all 26 shots he faced, 2.37 goals above what a typical goalie would have saved, and he absorbed every one of those late chances. The Sabres went 0 for 3 on the power play while Dallas cashed its lone conversion in two chances.
